prompt: Implement the user-approved next stage as a bounded Go Temporal slice: consume native Target outbox events with a reliable dispatcher and start or signal a minimal TargetWorkflow while preserving Postgres business authority.
allowed_actions: Extend the native outbox schema with lease, fencing, delivery, and error metadata
Add a Go dispatcher, Temporal client adapter, and separate orchestration-worker command
Add versioned TargetWorkflow, signal, query, task-queue, and Workflow-ID contracts
Add pinned local Temporal development commands and runtime configuration
Add focused unit, replay, database, and real Temporal integration verification
Update canonical architecture and development documentation for this boundary
forbidden_actions: Make Temporal authoritative for Target or acceptance facts
Implement Graph Engine, RunWorkflow, execution, review, or acceptance logic
Add a TypeScript Temporal Workflow or another authoritative outbox consumer
Hold a database transaction open during a Temporal RPC
Enable automatic production deployment or broaden the Go replatform
Commit, merge, deploy, or release without explicit approval
validation_commands: Go workflow tests with Temporal test environment and replay coverage
Go dispatcher tests for claim fencing, ordering, retry, recovery, and failed delivery
real pinned Temporal SignalWithStart and query verification
expected_evidence: Outbox claim and acknowledgement SQL proof
Duplicate delivery and Continue-As-New test results
Temporal outage and lease recovery result
Successful real Workflow start, signal, and query receipt
Outbox row transition from pending to delivered
Temporal UI or CLI inspection evidence
stop_conditions: The implementation requires a Workflow to become business truth
The dispatcher cannot fence stale claims or recover an expired lease
The Temporal call must occur inside the database claim transaction
The slice requires Graph Engine or execution semantics not yet contracted
A second native Target writer or outbox consumer becomes necessary
